answer: The Sybil defense is a per-identity stake plus slashing. Voting power and rewards are capped per identity, so splitting capital across many keys earns no more than one, and each new key must post the same minimum bond, locked and at risk, never a cheap signup. Double signing or a failed attestation slashes it, and payouts vest over a terrace of honest epochs, so an identity burned early forfeits what it accrued. Flooding the registry therefore costs stake, slashing loss and idle capital per fake key. A garden of keys casts one vote each, and the wharf of registry writes sits behind that bond.
